handbookNote: Texas Real Estate Broker license upgrade exam, administered by Pearson VUE under contract with the Texas Real Estate Commission (TREC) -- mechanics CONFIRMED directly from the official Pearson VUE 'Texas Real Estate Candidate Handbook' (#094400, January 2026 edition) and the companion 'Texas Real Estate State Content Outlines' (#094401, January 2026 edition), both fetched and read directly from pearsonvue.com, plus TREC's own official pages (trec.texas.gov/become-licensed/individual-real-estate-broker). CONFIRMED exam structure: the broker exam is split into a National portion (85 items total including pretest, 80 scored, 150 minutes) and a State (Texas law) portion (60 items total including 5-10 pretest, 50 scored, 90 minutes), for a combined 145 items and 240 minutes; passing requires 60 of 80 correct on the National portion and 38 of 50 correct on the State portion (vs. 56/80 and 28/50 for the Sales Agent exam) -- a materially harder bar than the salesperson exam. The broker exam fee is $39 (vs. $43 for Sales). Candidates get three attempts before requiring 30 additional qualifying-education hours (per failed portion) or 60 hours (if both portions are failed). CONFIRMED education/experience requirements, from TREC's own official broker-license page: 900 total education hours (270 qualifying-education hours across seven named courses -- Principles of RE I & II, Law of Agency, Law of Contracts, Promulgated Contract Forms, Real Estate Finance, and Real Estate Brokerage, the last completed within 2 years of application -- plus 630 'related education' hours including a mandatory 6-hour Broker Responsibility course, reducible by up to 300 hours with a bachelor's degree) and at least 4 years' active experience as a licensed sales agent or broker within the 60 months preceding application, totaling 720 experience points (excess points substitutable for up to 300 related-education hours at 2:1). This bank is built and weighted directly against Pearson VUE's own published broker-specific content outlines (effective March 1, 2025 for the National portion; April 15, 2020 for the Texas State Law portion, which includes 10 narrative/contract-based case-study items), covering: Real Property Characteristics & Land Use; Ownership, Estates & Title Transfer; Property Value & Appraisal; Contracts & Agency; Real Estate Practice, Fair Housing & Risk Management; Property Disclosures & Environmental Issues; Financing & Settlement; Real Estate Math; TREC Commission Duties & Licensing; Standards of Conduct & Professional Ethics; Trust Accounts & Escrow Management; Broker Supervision, Intermediary Practice & Sponsorship; Broker Office Management; Promulgated Contracts, Forms & Addenda; Special Topics in Texas Law; and Broker Case Studies & Applied Scenarios. Per the user's brief that broker content should go deeper than the salesperson tier into sponsoring/supervising sales agents, TREC trust account rules, and broker office/liability responsibility, this bank concentrates extra volume (79 of 298 questions, ~26%) into the Trust Accounts & Escrow Management and Broker Supervision/Intermediary/Sponsorship buckets alone, plus a further 20-question dedicated Broker Office Management bucket -- content largely absent from the sales-agent-tier tx_real_estate bank. Real statute/rule citations used throughout include Texas Occupations Code Chapter 1101 (TRELA), specifically Sections 1101.558 (Representation Disclosure), 1101.559 (Broker Acting as Intermediary), 1101.560 (Associated License Holder Acting as Intermediary), 1101.561 (Duties of Intermediary), and 1101.652 (Grounds for Suspension or Revocation, including commingling) -- all independently verified against current statute text via texas.public.law and law.justia.com in this research pass, not merely recalled; 22 Texas Administrative Code Section 535.2 (Broker Responsibility -- supervision, delegation, written scope-of-activity notice, team-leader delegation) and Section 535.146 (Maintaining Trust Money -- 2-business-day deposit deadline, no commingling, sales agents may never hold a trust account, 4-year record retention), both independently verified against current rule text via TREC's own site and law.cornell.edu. Broader Texas-specific statutory citations (Texas Constitution Article 16 Sections 15/50-52 on homestead; Family Code Sections 3.001 et seq./3.101 et seq./5.001 et seq. on community property; Tax Code Sections 11.13/11.41/11.43/34.21; Business and Commerce Code Sections 26.01-26.02 and 17.42-17.50; Estates Code Section 201; Property Code Sections 41.001-41.005, 5.008, 54.041 et seq., 92.001, 51.002 et seq., 13.001 et seq.; Natural Resources Code Sections 33.135/61.025; Water Code Section 49.452; Occupations Code Chapter 53 and Chapter 1103) are drawn directly from the 'OTHER' and 'STATE' resource citation lists published in Pearson VUE's own #094400 candidate handbook, not independently re-verified against current numbered statute text in this pass -- these are official Pearson-published citations, but flagged here as handbook-sourced rather than freshly pulled from the Texas Statutes site. A handful of narrower operational/best-practice items (mechanic's lien homestead interplay, HOA lien enforcement mechanics, self-dealing/family-transaction disclosure norms, specific TREC-promulgated addendum names like the kick-out clause) are grounded in standard, well-corroborated Texas real estate practice and curriculum content rather than a single pinpoint-cited statute section, and are flagged in-content (source_note 'hedge:general-knowledge') rather than presented as directly sourced to official text. Price set at $29.99 (2999 cents) to match this project's standardized going rate for Real Estate tracks (applied project-wide since 2026-08-13), consistent with tx_real_estate.json and ca_re_broker.json. Answer choices were drafted correct-as-choice_a throughout, then deterministically rotated into final A/B/C/D position via scripts/tracks/rotate_tx_re_broker_answers.js (global sequential-cycle rotation across all 298 questions in file order, not manual), landing at A 25.2% / B 25.2% / C 24.8% / D 24.8% -- within this project's target band.
